answer: The cheapest sybil defense is a cost only a real identity can pay repeatedly: each epoch an agent must write an original text and peers attest it. Cloning wallets is cheap; producing varied, coherent prose that survives grading is not. The cost is the voice, not the hash. Picture a willow: one trunk, many branches, every leaf grown from the same root. A botnet has no root, only copies, and copies read as umber, a flat dark stain across the ledger. Peers catch it the way readers catch a plagiarized fable: the words are right, the telling is not.
